key_insight: This review traces how materials information extraction has evolved from rule-based pipelines to multimodal LLMs and agentic systems that support materials discovery.
engineering_relevance: Automated literature extraction can populate materials databases and knowledge graphs, support research assistants, and inform closed-loop discovery when integrated with autonomous laboratories.
method: Review rule-based, NLP, transformer-encoder, and LLM extraction approaches.
Examine extraction across text, tables, and figures.
Assess datasets, accuracy, computational costs, and pipeline design.
evidence_signal: The review critically assesses generated datasets and extraction performance, but the abstract reports no quantitative benchmarks and highlights scarce reliable evaluation datasets.
watch_item: Reliable sample-level linking of structure, properties, processing, and performance remains an open challenge, compounded by non-standard terminology across modalities.
paper_title: Automated Materials Data and Knowledge Extraction using Machine Learning and Large Language Models
